authority.claim: Normative identities, state propositions, legal joins, and checked journeys only; no runtime implementation or migration.

request_state.law: One canonical request entry advances on orthogonal axes; no total phase value stands in for the full state.

one_authority.law: One canonical semantic owner does not require one object, actor, global lock, or mutable store.

generic_boundary.currentness_law: Currentness is opaque evidence minted and validated only by its owning authority.

axes.proposition: Whether the application service is able to accept new execution work.
Whether every resource owned by the request has reached a known terminal or released state.
Whether one physical or logical protocol connection is open, closing, or closed.
Whether cancellation, deadline, supersession, or shutdown control has been requested or applied.
Whether application work is rejected, queued, running, or completed.
Preparation, admission, writer commitment, flush commitment, or failure of one output obligation.
Whether an observed message satisfies the protocol envelope and message-shape contract.
The protocol-defined server lifecycle, independent from connection and task settlement.
Whether a terminal result is current and committed to the causal publication order.
Whether all runtime tasks owned by the relevant session or request have reached known settlement.
Which exactly-once terminal cause owns the request outcome.
Whether capacity is reserved and one canonical request obligation is registered.

boundary_terms.name: ApplicationCompletion
boundary_terms.proposition: An application invocation returned, failed, or otherwise stopped producing application work.

boundary_terms.name: DeliveryFate
boundary_terms.proposition: The writer and transport outcome for one output obligation.

boundary_terms.name: TerminalDecision
boundary_terms.proposition: The exactly-once terminal authority selected the request cause that owns all later publication attempts.

boundary_terms.name: TerminalSignal
boundary_terms.proposition: One candidate cause asks terminal authority to decide an outcome.
boundary_terms.owner: The source of the candidate cause.

ambiguous_terms.reason: Acceptance has several authorities; name the exact admission or commitment proposition.
Name the exact identity and axis instead of collapsing registration, execution, output, or task ownership.
Execution admission and output admission are different axes.
Protocol exit, connection closure, task settlement, and request cleanup are distinct.
Application, writer, flush, task, and cleanup completion are not interchangeable.
Channel admission, write, flush, and client consumption are distinct propositions.
Name whether the request is registered, queued, running, awaiting terminal selection, or awaiting cleanup.
Causal publication commitment is not writer admission or external consumption.
A candidate terminal signal is not the selected terminal decision or settled delivery fate.
